# Dedup / No-Repeat Policy

**The "no repeat task" centrepiece of eq-sparks.** The platform must produce strong output under budget — even on Haiku — by never doing the same work twice. Not the same generation, not the same fetch, not the same stage, not the same line of code. This policy is the contract that makes "no repeated work and aggressive caching" real.

There are two distinct kinds of repeat we kill:

- **Repeat CODE** — two MFEs hand-roll the same table; a domain re-implements a shaper the design system already provides. Killed by mechanisms 1 and 4.
- **Repeat WORK** — re-fetching the same ADO item, re-running the same `contract-diff`, re-doing a stage that already passed on a previous run. Killed by mechanisms 2, 3, and 5.

> One-line buyer's promise: **re-running the same PBI costs near-zero on everything already satisfied, and a brand-new PBI never re-creates code that already exists.**

---

## The five mechanisms

### 1. DNA pre-check — classify BEFORE you generate (kills repeat CODE)

Every build agent (`@codegen`, `@mfe`, `@state`, `@design-system`, `@domain-folder`, `@bff-shaper`, `@downstream-connector`, `@contract-publisher`) MUST run the **`dna-precheck`** skill before emitting a single line of code. No precheck → `@critic` returns **FAIL**.

`dna-precheck` cross-scans the estate for each artifact the task needs and classifies it:

| Verdict | Meaning | Where it looks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **REUSE** | An equivalent already exists; consume it as-is. | `eq-one-design-system`, `eq-one-shared`, sibling MFEs (`eq-one-saye-mfe` / `eq-one-sip-mfe` / `eq-one-shares-mfe`), other `src/domains/<name>/` folders |
| **EXTEND** | A near-match exists; widen/adapt it rather than fork it. | same surfaces as above |
| **CREATE** | Genuinely new; nothing comparable exists. | greenfield |

The DNA report is the build agent's input. A `CREATE` verdict on something that scanning shows already exists is a `@critic` blocker — the agent must downgrade to `REUSE`/`EXTEND`.

### 2. Skill-output cache — identical fetches/scans never re-run (kills repeat WORK)

Read-only skills are cached per run, keyed by **`(skill_id, version, input_hash)`** via the **`cache-lookup`** primitive. Two calls with the same key return the first result instead of re-executing. This covers `ado-context`, `figma-context`, `contract-diff`, and cross-repo searches.

NEVER cached (per **cache-policy**): writes, test runs, `self-evaluate`, and raw LLM completions. Caching a write or a test would mask drift — strictly forbidden.

See **cache-policy** for TTLs, the opt-in cross-run cache for stable PBI metadata, and key construction.

### 3. Idempotent task ledger — completed stages/sub-tasks SKIP on re-run (kills repeat WORK)

`@supervisor` records every completed stage and sub-task to an append-only ledger at:

```
.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/ledger.jsonl
```

Each entry carries a **content hash** of the satisfying output (schema in **memory-schema**):

```jsonc
{ "task_id": "stage.bff.shape-response", "status": "done",
  "content_hash": "sha256:…", "artifact_paths": ["src/domains/payments/…"],
  "model_tier": "sonnet", "ts": "2026-06-13T…" }
```

On any re-run or `/resume`, `@supervisor` replays the ledger first:

- Task present, `status: done`, and inputs hash unchanged → **SKIP** (no agent launched, no tokens spent).
- Inputs changed (different acceptance criteria, drifted contract) → the hash differs → task is **re-run**, and only that task.

This is what makes Flow 3 (cloud → IDE handoff via `/resume`) cheap: `/resume` reads the ledger and continues from the first unsatisfied task without re-fetching ADO/Figma.

### 4. Reuse precedence REUSE > EXTEND > CREATE — enforced, not suggested (kills repeat CODE)

The DNA verdict is binding, in strict precedence:

1. **REUSE** an existing artifact wherever possible.
2. **EXTEND** the nearest match if reuse isn't a clean fit.
3. **CREATE** only when nothing comparable exists.

Enforcement:

- **`@decision`** resolves every reuse-vs-create fork with a logged, defensible rationale (vague placement, near-duplicate, "is this shared yet?").
- **`@shared-curator`** is the standing enforcer of "no repeat code": it detects duplicated/common code across MFEs and **MOVES it to `eq-one-shared`** using the **`move-to-shared`** skill (which rewrites all importers), and **flags dead code for removal**.
- Common stores follow the same rule via **`@state`** → `eq-one-shared`.
- UI MUST consume `eq-one-design-system`; **`@design-system`** BLOCKS hand-rolled equivalents of components the design system already provides.
- **`@critic`** FAILs any diff that duplicates code which should have been reused, extended, or moved to shared.

Anything reused MOVES to `eq-one-shared`; child MFEs MUST NOT duplicate code. Placement obeys **path-policy**.

### 5. Prompt-prefix stability — amortise the stable context (kills repeat WORK)

Every agent invocation orders its context as a stable prefix followed by the volatile task:

```
[ platform/guardrail context | agent spec | volatile task ]
```

Because the platform + agent-spec prefix is byte-identical across a run, Anthropic prompt caching reuses it instead of re-billing it on each turn (5-min TTL, per **cache-policy**). Agents MUST NOT interleave volatile, per-task content into the prefix — doing so breaks the cache and silently re-bills the whole context.

---

## Concrete before / after — same PBI, re-run

PBI "Add ISA balance card to the SIP MFE", fanning out across `@mfe`, `@design-system`, `@state`, `@bff-shaper`, `@contract-publisher`, `@contract`, then the governance trio.

### First run (cold)
- `ado-context` + `figma-context` fetched and **cached**.
- `dna-precheck` finds the balance card pattern already in `eq-one-design-system` → **REUSE** (no new component authored); the ISA store is new → **CREATE** in `eq-one-shared`.
- BFF shaper + `contract-publisher` produce the contract; `@contract` aligns FE types via `contract-diff`.
- `@critic` PASS; `@supervisor` writes every stage to the ledger with content hashes.
- **Cost:** full — fetches, generation, tests, reviews, governance.

### Second run (same PBI, nothing changed)
- `@supervisor` replays the ledger → all `task_id`s present, hashes unchanged → **every stage SKIPPED**.
- `ado-context` / `figma-context` / `contract-diff` would hit the **skill-output cache** even if a stage did re-run — no re-fetch.
- DNA pre-check would re-verify **REUSE** of the design-system card → no duplicate component.
- Prompt prefix is cache-hot for the few orchestration turns that do run.
- **Cost:** **near-zero** — a ledger replay plus a handful of cache-hot orchestration tokens. No generation, no fetches, no tests re-run.

### Third run (one acceptance criterion changed)
- The changed AC flips the `input_hash` for exactly the BFF-shaper + contract sub-tasks → **those two re-run**; everything else **SKIPPED** from the ledger.
- **Cost:** the delta only — proportional to what actually changed, not to the size of the PBI.

---

## Enforcement summary

| # | Mechanism | Owner / enforcer | Hard gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | DNA pre-check before generation | build agents + `@critic` | FAIL if missing or mis-classified |
| 2 | Skill-output cache `(skill_id, version, input_hash)` | `cache-lookup` (cache-policy) | never cache writes/tests/self-eval/LLM |
| 3 | Idempotent ledger w/ content hash | `@supervisor` (memory-schema) | satisfied tasks SKIP on re-run/`/resume` |
| 4 | REUSE > EXTEND > CREATE | `@decision`, `@shared-curator`, `@design-system`, `@state`; `@critic` | FAIL on avoidable duplication |
| 5 | Stable prompt prefix | every agent (cache-policy) | no volatile content in the prefix |

**Net guarantee:** no agent regenerates code that already exists, no skill re-fetches the same input, and no stage that already passed runs again. The cheap model stays cheap because the platform refuses to repeat itself.
